etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Borrowed from French éponyme (“eponymous person”), from the nominalization of the adjective éponyme (“eponymous”), from Latin epōnymus (adjective), from Ancient Greek ἐπώνῠμος (epṓnŭmos, adjective), from ἐπί (epí, “upon, epi-”) +‎ ὄνυμα (ónuma, “name”) +‎ -ος (-os, suffix forming compound adjectives (often nominalizable)). By surface analysis, epi- +‎ -onym.
senses: A person who gave or supposedly gave their name to a people, place, institution, etc. [from 17th c.]
